stories.headline: Earthquake of 6.9 magnitude hits near Ozernovskiy in Russia
stories.title: Earthquake of 6.9 magnitude hits near Ozernovskiy in Russia
stories.summary: Moscow, Oct 16: An earthquake of 6.9 magnitude struck 76 km northeast of Ozernovskiy in Russia on Friday, the US Geological Survey said. The epicentre, with a depth of 143.2 km, was initially determined to be at 52.01 degrees north latitude and 157.25 degrees east longitude, it said. A perceptible earthquake with an intensity of up to four magnitude points has been registered in Kamchatka, Russia's state-run TASS news agency reported, citing the Kamchatka branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences’ Geophysical Service. “Instrumental intensity in Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky amounted to up to four points,” scientists said. Scientists estimated its magnitude at 6.5 first, but later revised it to 6.9. It was felt as a magnitude-5 earthquake in the region, it said. “According to verified information, the magnitude of this seismic event was 6.9. Its epicentre was located on land, 156 km southwest of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, at the depth of 138 km. In Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, it was felt as a magnitude-5 earthquake,” seismologists said. A number of residents of the region’s administrative centre evacuated from their apartments because of tremors, it said. Inside residential buildings, the earthquake caused light fixtures to swing violently, doors to slam shut, and tableware to rattle. According to eyewitnesses, the tremor, which occurred at 3:36 pm local time (3:36 a.m. GMT), continued for about one minute.

stories.headline: Farooq Abdullah slams IAS officer over misconduct, demands his removal from J&K
stories.title: Farooq Abdullah slams IAS officer over misconduct, demands his removal from J&K
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 16: National Conference president Dr Farooq Abdullah on Friday said he felt ashamed after watching a video of an IAS officer misbehaving with a woman officer, calling his conduct unbecoming of a senior administrative official. Speaking to reporters in Srinagar, Dr Farooq Abdullah, said the language used by the officer was unacceptable and reflected a lack of the discipline and professionalism expected of an IAS officer. “The language he used with the woman officer was extremely inappropriate. He should be reprimanded. This shows that he lacks the manners and conduct expected of an officer,” he said, as per the news agency—Kashmir News Observer (KNO). Dr Farooq said officers were appointed to serve the public, listen to their grievances and resolve their problems rather than insult or humiliate them. “People want to express their grievances, and officers should hear them patiently. Instead, he directly said, ‘Get out, get out.’ This is completely wrong. He should be removed from Jammu and Kashmir,” he said. Expressing dismay over the incident, Abdullah said, “When I saw the incident on social media today, I felt ashamed. His behaviour was completely unbecoming of an IAS officer. He has put the entire administrative community in an embarrassing position.” Asked whether such incidents occurred during his tenure as Chief Minister, Abdullah said no officer or minister had the right to insult people. “Whether someone is an officer or a minister, they are here to serve the people and resolve their difficulties, not to insult or abuse them,” he said. Backing Chief Minister Omar Abdullah’s remarks that such an incident would not have occurred had Jammu and Kashmir retained its statehood, Farooq Abdullah said he would have taken stronger action against the officer. “He would not merely have been attached. He would have been thrown out. If I had been in office, he would not have remained in Jammu and Kashmir for more than a few minutes. I would have put him back on a plane and sent him away,” he said. He said the incident reflected changes in the administrative functioning of Jammu and Kashmir since 2019. On protests in Delhi, Abdullah welcomed the demonstrations, saying a new wave was emerging against what he described as autocracy. “I think these protests are very good. A new wave is beginning against autocracy and against a Hitlerian way of life,” he said. Dr Farooq futher urged US President Donald Trump to recognise dialogue and negotiations as the only viable means of resolving disputes. “Let us hope that Trump realises that war is not a solution. Negotiation is the way to resolve conflicts. You are not going to win through war. You will only end up killing people, and innocent people will lose their lives,” he said.—(KNO)

stories.headline: Congress, allies seeking Bangladesh-like regime change: Rajnath
stories.title: Congress, allies seeking Bangladesh-like regime change: Rajnath
stories.summary: Lucknow, Oct 16: Union Minister Rajnath Singh on Friday lashed out at the Congress and its allies over the protests in the national capital, accusing them of seeking a regime change along the lines of Bangladesh and using the energy of youth to spread "anarchy". Addressing a press conference here, Singh asserted that democracy does not give anyone the licence to create disorder or undermine the credibility of constitutional institutions. "It appears that the Congress and its political allies, directly and through their supporting organisations, are trying to use the energy of the youth to fuel political confrontation and spread anarchy instead of channelling it towards constructive work and nation-building," he said. "The youth of the country are being made pawns in the politics of anarchy," he stated. Singh alleged that the Congress and its allies want a change of government in India along the lines of Bangladesh. "They openly say at press conferences that they have drawn inspiration from Bangladesh for regime change, while another speaks openly about bringing down the government. This makes it clear that their only agenda is to dismantle democratic institutions and set the country on fire," he said referring to the uprising in Bangladesh in 2024 that toppled the Sheikh Hasina government. The defence minister said the use of terms such as "regime change" showed that the opposition's campaign was not about electoral reforms or issues related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. His remarks come amid massive protests in the national capital by opposition parties and civil society groups demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR process. Opposition leaders have alleged that the exercise lacks transparency and could exclude eligible voters. Referring to the Supreme Court's observations on Thursday, Singh said Gandhi and his allies need to understand that democracy does not permit attempts to create anarchy, undermine constitutional institutions or obstruct India's development. "Respecting the law is also essential to maintaining law and order. India's democratic institutions cannot be sacrificed at the altar of political self-interest," he said. Singh added that falsehoods, anger, attempts to malign institutions and political opportunism could not obstruct India's development. He advised Gandhi to respect the people's mandate and introspect on his political role instead of pursuing what he called "politics of destruction" in the name of protecting democracy. "India's future is everyone's responsibility. We must choose the path of dialogue and nation-building, not confrontation," Singh said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court seeks Centre’s reply on social media age limits for children
stories.title: Supreme Court seeks Centre’s reply on social media age limits for children
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 16 : The Supreme Court on Friday issued notice to the Centre on a plea seeking a comprehensive and enforceable regulatory framework to protect children from the risks associated with social media platforms, including age-based restrictions on access and safeguards against online exploitation. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi issued notice on the petition filed by The Emerald Heights International School and its Director (Academics), Siddharth Singh Girnar, and tagged it with a pending petition raising a similar issue. The apex court has listed the matter for further hearing on December 3. The petition, filed against the Union of India, the Ministry of Women and Child Development, the Ministry of Law and Justice, and the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights, raises concerns over unrestricted access to commercial social media platforms by children and the alleged inadequacy of the existing legal and regulatory framework to address the risks posed by their use. The plea contends that social media platforms generally prescribe a self-declared minimum age of 13 years, which does not correspond to the protection accorded to children under Indian law. It refers to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, which recognises every person below 18 years of age as a child and provides for enhanced safeguards, including verifiable parental consent and restrictions on tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising. “The present framework remains fragmented, incomplete and inadequately operationalised,” the petition stated, arguing that there is no uniform and enforceable child-safety regime governing age verification, prevention of underage access, parental involvement and platform accountability. The petitioners have claimed that children are increasingly exposed to cyberbullying, harassment, harmful online content and unwanted contact from strangers through social media. They have also raised concerns over sleep deprivation, diminished concentration, anxiety, low self-esteem and declining academic engagement associated with prolonged social media use. The plea further stated that parents have expressed concerns over their children's excessive phone use, late-night exposure, online interactions and the risk of bullying, grooming and exploitation, while finding it difficult to supervise or restrict access to such platforms. The petition has sought directions to the Centre and the authorities concerned to formulate and notify a dedicated regulatory framework providing for reliable, proportionate and privacy-preserving age verification, graded and age-appropriate access, restrictions on harmful content and mandatory privacy settings for accounts belonging to children. It has also sought safeguards against grooming, sexual solicitation, cyberbullying, harassment and the circulation of intimate or private images, including effective reporting mechanisms, prompt removal of harmful material and preservation of evidence in accordance with law. In the alternative, the petitioners have sought directions to prescribe and enforce restrictions on children's creation and use of social media platforms if other safeguards are found insufficient to address the risks. --IANS

stories.title: India GDP to grow 7.1-7.3% in FY27 on private investment revival: Deloitte
stories.summary: The Indian economy is expected to grow by 7.1-7.3 per cent in the current fiscal, with a sustained revival in private investment providing an additional source of demand, Deloitte India said on Friday. However, geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices and trade disruptions pose risks to the growth outlook, it added. Deloitte India Economist Rumki Majumdar said over the past decade, India's growth has rested on resilient household spending and sustained investment push in public infrastructure. Businesses now have better connectivity, healthier balance sheets, and higher capacity utilisation, which strengthens the case for expansion. "The question is whether these conditions will encourage private investment to play a larger role in boosting growth in the coming years. Recent indicators offer grounds for optimism. Gross fixed capital formation grew by 11.9 per cent in the first quarter of FY 2026-27, its fastest expansion in four years," Majumdar said. Deloitte Economic Outlook

Senior advocate Siddharth Luthra mentioned the matter before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Friday, seeking an urgent hearing, citing the registration of an FIR and the possibility of coercive action against the CPM leader.

stories.headline: India may raise fuel prices in November, says economist Alexandra Hermann Prasad
stories.title: India may raise fuel prices in November, says economist Alexandra Hermann Prasad
stories.summary: If authorities do not announce a fuel price increase in November, Oxford Economics’ inflation projections could decline by 10-30 basis points in the coming quarters.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'fuel price' in summary weight 24
article_sentences: The proposed increase could be around half the magnitude of the cumulative 7.5% hike implemented in May, the only period when retail fuel prices rose in response to the war in the Middle East.

Such an increase could push retail inflation to 6.2% in the October-December quarter and 6.5% in the first three months of 2027, both exceeding the Reserve Bank of India’s inflation target range of 2-6%, it said.
Oxford Economics’ projections are higher than the central bank’s estimates.
In its monetary policy review earlier this month, the RBI projected inflation at 6% for the October-December quarter, easing to 5.7% in January-March.
Oxford Economics expects price pressures to intensify next year, forecasting inflation at 5.4% for the financial year ending March, compared with the RBI’s projection of 5.2%.
If authorities do not announce a fuel price increase in November, Oxford Economics’ inflation projections could decline by 10-30 basis points in the coming quarters, the report added.

Inflation would nevertheless remain elevated, potentially prompting the RBI to raise interest rates by 25 basis points each at its December and February policy meetings, following a quarter-point increase in October.
Inflation rose to 5.54% in September, its highest level since late 2024, from 4.83% in August.
Hermann Prasad said the RBI’s recent measures in the currency market should help contain rupee volatility.
However, elevated oil prices and persistent external financing pressures mean intervention alone is unlikely to ensure lasting currency stability.

She also said widening protests over allegations of electoral malpractice were unlikely to materially affect economic growth, as disruption had largely remained confined to Delhi and was too limited to have a significant impact.

Separately, aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said that discussions are underway with airlines to ensure that ticket prices are kept reasonable, which is a challenging task given the unstable jet fuel prices.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court today stayed the ongoing trial before a Bhopal sessions court in the unnatural death case of Twisha Sharma.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi issued notice to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), her husband Samarth Singh and mother-in-law Giribala Singh on a plea by her father seeking transfer of the proceedings from Madhya Pradesh to Delhi.
Advocate Abhijeet Sinha appeared Twisha's father Navnidhi Sharma.

He has sought the transfer due to an apprehension that the case would not receive a fair trial in Madhya Pradesh because Giribala Singh, one of the accused, is a former judge and is influential in the state.
He sought the transfer of the trial to Delhi, submitting that he is settled in Delhi-NCR.

The CBI subsequently took over the probe.
Twisha, a 33-year-old woman, was discovered dead at her matrimonial home in Bhopal on May 12, 2026, around five months after her marriage to Samarth Singh on December 9, 2025.
Her husband, Samarth Singh, a lawyer, and mother-in-law, Giribala Singh, a retired district judge, are facing prosecution in the case.

The initial FIR was registered under Sections 80(2) (dowry death), 85 (cruelty by husband or his relatives) and 3(5) (common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, which deal with giving or taking dowry and demanding dowry, respectively.

stories.title: Supreme Court asks High Court to consider plea against Centre’s decision to take over Delhi Gymkhana Club

reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (October 5, 2026) asked the Delhi High Court to consider a plea by 11 members of the Delhi Gymkhana Club, who had challenged the Centre's decision to take over the club's 27.3-acre premises and the subsequent eviction proceedings.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana was told by senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the members, that the Delhi High Court had refused to entertain their plea on the ground that only the club could challenge the Centre's decision.
Mr. Singh said the High Court had asked the members to get a clarification from the Supreme Court that they could also move the plea there.
The Court permitted them to move the High Court, subject to objections that may be raised by the other side regarding maintainability and other legal oppositions.

Mr. Singh, appearing for the 11 members, had earlier told the Bench that a Central government-nominated committee was presently managing the club, and that it could not fight a legal battle with the government.

On September 3, 2026, the Centre, in a separate case, told the Delhi High Court that it would not take any coercive action until September 16, 2026, against the club in relation to its eviction from the premises on Safdarjung Road.

The High Court was hearing pleas by club member Vijay Khurana and others, seeking a stay on the June 29, 2026, show-cause notice for eviction issued to the club's management by an estate officer of the Land and Development Office (L&DO).

Vipin Aggarwal and ten other club members, in their petition filed through lawyer Nitin Saluja, sought the quashing of the resumption notification issued by the L&DO on May 22, 2026, and the show-cause notice issued by the estate officer on June 29, 2026.

stories.headline: IMD: Heavy rain in Keralam, South Karnataka, TN, Puducherry for 4 days from Thursday
stories.title: IMD: Heavy rain in Keralam, South Karnataka, TN, Puducherry for 4 days from Thursday
stories.summary: Watch for low-pressure system over south-east Bay of Bengal withdrawn after parent circulation disappears, but South Peninsula is entering a consequential wet phase in seasonal calendar
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The north-east monsoon could set in over the South Peninsula within next two days, even as the India Meteorological Department (IMD) appeared on Monday to have dropped its watch for Tuesday for a low-pressure area that the south-east Bay of Bengal was thought to come up with.

The trigger for the emerging wet spell may instead be a trough linking cyclonic circulations over the south-west and central Bay off Sri Lanka coast with the parent circulation over the south Andaman Sea.
This circulation has merged into this trough, which could help channel the easterlies and usher in the north-east monsoon.
The 2026 season is set to open with a six-day wet spell from Wednesday/Thursday, with isolated heavy rainfall forecast over several parts of the South Peninsula.
Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are likely to bear the brunt of the initial spell, followed by Kerala and Mahe from Thursday, an IMD said on Monday.

The rain belt is expected to extend across coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and South Interior Karnataka for four days from Thursday; Coastal Karnataka, North Interior Karnataka and Rayalaseema for three days from Friday; and Telangana on Saturday.
Isolated to scattered, and at times fairly widespread to widespread overlapping rainfall is forecast at many places across these regions during these days, with pockets of heavy rain.
Historical performance of the north-east monsoon shows the meteorological subdivision of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal received its highest seasonal rainfall in 2015 (floods) and 2021.
The absolute lowest point was 2016 (-62 per cent).
It remains the only subdivision in India where rainfall during north-east (October to December) monsoon rainfall exceeds that during the south-west monsoon (June to September).
For Kerala and Mahe, 2011-2025 has delivered a highly volatile season marked by excesses and severe deficits in 2016 and 2023.

The subdivision logged exceptionally high excess in 2021 and 2023 (+27 per cent) that contrasted heavily with dry spells during strong El Niño interludes where its interior catchments have routinely failed.

stories.headline: India received 15% below normal monsoon rainfall this year: IMD
stories.title: India received 15% below normal monsoon rainfall this year: IMD
stories.summary: Goa receives 196.68 cm rainfall, which is the highest in the country, while Punjab reports 28 cm, the lowest
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India received 76.86 cm rainfall between June 4 and October 15 when the south-west monsoon was active over the country, which is 15 per cent below its long period average of 90.63 cm, according to India Meteorological Department (IMD) data.
The south-west monsoon, after its onset over Keralam on June 4, withdrew from the entire country on October 15.

During this period, except Andaman and Nicobar islands which reported 1 per cent surplus rainfall, all the meteorological sub-divisions in the south peninsula region were deficient with a shortfall between 23 per cent and 46 per cent.
As the north-east monsoon has now set in, these sub-divisions look forward to getting some rains to help the crops in winter season, particularly in non-irrigated areas.
In Central India where monsoon rainfall was 6 per cent below normal, except Maharashtra and Goa, which were deficient, all other states had either normal or excess rainfall.
Maharashtra has reported 23 per cent deficit and Goa 36 per cent.
On the other hand, Odisha received 23 per cent surplus rains, whereas Chhattisgarh 2 per cent shortfall.
Madhya Pradesh had 7 per cent deficit and Gujarat 12 per cent below normal.
The north-west India too received 6 per cent below normal rains like Central India.

Among the major agricultural states in this region, Punjab (-37 per cent), Haryana (-21 per cent) and Rajasthan (-24 per cent) reported deficient rainfall while Uttar Pradesh (+6 per cent) had normal precipitation.
The east and north-east region was 27 per cent deficient as Arunachal Pradesh (-45 per cent), Assam (-29 per cent), Bihar (-32 per cent) and Meghalaya (-61 per cent) had less rainfall.
But, West Bengal has reported 2 per cent deficit and Jharkhand 6 per cent deficit rainfall between June 4 and October 15.

opening: India received 76.86 cm rainfall between June 4 and October 15 when the south-west monsoon was active over the country, which is 15 per cent below its long period average of 90.63 cm, according to India Meteorological Department (IMD) data.
The south-west monsoon, after its onset over Keralam on June 4, withdrew from the entire country on October 15.
body: During this period, except Andaman and Nicobar islands which reported 1 per cent surplus rainfall, all the meteorological sub-divisions in the south peninsula region were deficient with a shortfall between 23 per cent and 46 per cent.
As the north-east monsoon has now set in, these sub-divisions look forward to getting some rains to help the crops in winter season, particularly in non-irrigated areas.
In Central India where monsoon rainfall was 6 per cent below normal, except Maharashtra and Goa, which were deficient, all other states had either normal or excess rainfall.
Maharashtra has reported 23 per cent deficit and Goa 36 per cent.
